summary.text: Nikki Lucas is the incumbent Democratic Assembly Member for District 60, first elected in a February 2022 special election. A more-than-30-year resident of Starrett City, she founded The People First Democratic Club and The People First Education Fund before entering the Assembly, and she has sponsored reparations bills including the Freedmen's Bureau Act.

paragraphs.text: According to the Assembly biography, Nikki Lucas became involved in civic life at age 8 as the child of parents who were active in their community.
She earned a degree in liberal arts from the Borough of Manhattan Community College and continued her studies at Syracuse University, majoring in policy studies and conflict resolution.
Lucas has lived in Starrett City for more than 30 years and describes herself as an advocate for East New York residents, having implemented programs intended to uplift Brooklyn residents.
She founded and served as president of The People First Democratic Club and The People First Education Fund, and she has been affiliated with HealthyNYC.
In 2021 she ran in the Democratic primary for New York City Council District 42 and lost to Charles Barron in the ranked-choice tabulation.

Lucas won the February 15, 2022 special election for Assembly District 60 with 79.8% of the vote, over Keron Alleyne (Working Families Party) and Marvin King (Republican/Conservative), then won a full term in November 2022 and was re-elected in 2024.
Her 2025-2026 committee assignments are Aging; Economic Development, Job Creation, Commerce and Industry; Energy; Health; Housing; and Labor.
She is the Assembly sponsor of A05603, the New York State American Freedmen Task Force on Reparations Remedies Act, and A08284, the New York State Freedmen's Bureau Act.
